llm.summary: This skill does what it says at a high level, but it installs an indefinite cron job that repeatedly contacts EvoMap without confirmation, removal controls, or reliable duplicate handling.

dimensions.detail: Shell, curl, environment variables, and network access are proportionate for a heartbeat-maintenance skill, but the cron job may not inherit the required environment variables and can keep running while failing every 15 minutes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains a Markdown skill file and one local shell script; I found no remote payload download, package installation, tool hijacking, or privilege-escalation install step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The setup path modifies the user's crontab for recurring execution, but the skill does not provide an explicit confirmation prompt, disable/uninstall command, exact managed entry disclosure, or bounded lifetime. It also asks users to export EVOMAP_SECRET without meaningful secret-handling guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The setup command installs user-level cron persistence every 15 minutes and writes logs under /tmp. The behavior is partly disclosed as permanent automatic maintenance, but lifecycle controls and idempotent ownership marking are missing.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose is automatic EvoMap node maintenance, and the bundled script checks status and sends heartbeats to https://evomap.ai, which matches that purpose. The documentation also claims automatic, permanent operation and point-earning benefits.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want a user-level cron job that runs every 15 minutes and sends authenticated EvoMap heartbeat data to evomap.ai. Before using setup, inspect your crontab, understand how to remove the entry manually, and avoid placing EVOMAP_SECRET where it may be logged, committed, or exposed in shell history.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell use is expected because the skill is implemented as maintainer.sh, but the artifact does not clearly declare the required command authority or persistence implications up front.
[SQP-2] expected: EVOMAP_SECRET is needed for authenticated heartbeats, but the documentation does not explain that it is used as a bearer token or provide safe handling guidance.
[E1] expected: The outbound POST to evomap.ai is the core heartbeat function, not unrelated exfiltration; the concern is disclosure and credential handling, not a hidden destination.
[RA2] expected: Recurring execution is aligned with automatic maintenance, but installing it into crontab creates durable background behavior without confirmation or removal support.
[T06] expected: The cron persistence is real and purpose-related, but it is high-impact enough to require review because it is indefinite and lacks lifecycle controls.
[T09] unexpected: The duplicate check searches for a marker that the installed cron line does not include, so repeated setup runs can accumulate scheduled jobs.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only text matches the artifact's apparent audience and is not a security concern by itself, though users who do not read Chinese may miss important behavior details.
